title: Prove exact least replication for compatible width menus (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Prove exact least common replication for chronological batches supplied by finite menus of compatible completed program widths. Claim type: scoped written mathematical proof with exact finite corroboration. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas.

```text
whole menu invocations at each separate cut
  -> additive width monoids
  -> certified least size in each residue
  -> bounded search for the least common replication
```

For two cuts containing N and N+1 jobs, with the same menu {N,N+1}, mixed-width replication is exactly one. Either single menu width used at both cuts needs replication at least N; width N attains it. The conditional productive-width reduction factor is therefore exactly N, for every N>=2. One eleven-job cut with menu {4,7} also admits a literal (1,1) invocation partition at replication one.

The changed premise is a menu of completed widths. Mihir Srivastava / mihir-s-05's PR4507 supplies the chronological contract and earlier single-width LCM theorem. PR4892 and PR6612 retain a prescribed single width per rank. This result changes neither their rank inventory nor their stopping height and does not audit or replay their results. Apéry sets, numerical semigroups, shortest paths and gcd/LCM arithmetic are classical. Credit Jacob Alan Sussman, zxv, codyw912, Cinna Davis and Ryanson Jonathan for the retained compiler/native lineage.

Only seven files under `research/mixed-width-batching` are added. Scientific base and refreshed canonical main are `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`, priority revision 8, selected PR6030. [Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19376781).

## Evidence

Before, the fixed policy requires a width-divisibility LCM. After, the new theorem and optimizer admit sums of compatible invocation widths, provide literal partition witnesses, and reject gcd-only and cross-cut-pooling relaxations.

- All 175 menus of one through three distinct widths in 1..10 pass 44,975 exact membership comparisons against a separate total-size dynamic program.
- Exhaustive positive-integer search agrees on 6,264 declared systems: 1,400 one-cut, 3,136 two-cut and 1,728 three-cut systems. The oracle uses neither residue tables nor the replication formula.
- N=2..24 strict-family schedules execute 10,718 bank triples, including the best single-width comparator. Every complete output retains its dirty coordinate and every cut completes. A synthetic complete linear-cost bill preserves normalized cost.
- Sixteen malformed boundaries, six residue-certificate corruptions, gcd/pooling controls and five capacity fixtures pass. Two disposable corrupted implementations reject, respectively at least-replication and membership comparisons.
- CPython 3.12.15 warning-strict normal and optimized direct checks pass in 0.22s and 0.23s locally. These are check durations, not speedup claims. Both registered commands have 120-second limits and pass.
- Registered metadata/replay, all seven committed bytes and executable modes, and full declared source ancestry pass at `bd728a5c8d09599072a98503ca7741d934ecfa74`. Official export integrity and declared-input checks pass. Both standalone modes pass in the read-only Git-free export with empty PATH and all eight exported files unchanged. Receipts are generated from actual checks and bind every package file by SHA256.

From the worktree root, using the exact local interpreter path or another CPython 3.12 installation:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -X dev -B research/mixed-width-batching/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -X dev -B research/mixed-width-batching/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/mixed-width-batching
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/mixed-width-batching --check-source-history --check-modes
```

Expected markers are PASS_MIXED_WIDTH_BATCHING, PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE and PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES. No predecessor scientific executable is imported or replayed.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal conclusion rests on the written proof; the listed finite domains corroborate it. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

Menus must actually contain compatible completed programs with the same per-job endpoint and appropriate ownership/return contracts. No physical native menu is supplied. Widths obtained only by copying one smallest program do not provide the strict improvement. Normalized cost preservation requires a common complete cost per productive job; unequal costs, fixed invocation overheads and routing must be charged separately.

This is a conditional invocation-policy theorem, not a complete compiler, supplier admission, practical speedup, new kappa or complete multiplication theorem. Storage extent, native realization, frames, movement, precision/tape, stock, analytic recovery and all five selected framework assumptions remain separate. Selected scientific replay, native suites, Lean and Docker were not run. Every registered package command ran locally; none was deferred to hosted CI.

## Open next questions

- Exhibit two actual nondividing same-rank widths with matching arbitrary-input, owned-return and complete-cost contracts. First pin both programs and their full invoices; that physical menu is missing here.
- Determine the replication/cost frontier for an explicitly priced finite menu. Begin with the residue feasibility certificates; unequal per-job costs and fixed invocation fees are outside this theorem.

## Related open work

- PR6612 proves polynomial widths for a homogeneous single-width chronological recurrence. This result changes to compatible width menus and computes no competing value for its rank-10 or all-rank fixtures.
- PR6384 weakens a mirror-capacity gate for a capped-flow compiler. This result optimizes whole-invocation replication under fixed compatible menus and does not compute its capacity ratio or compiler saving.

Live open PRs, recent account work, Discussions, local reservations, full-main distinctive README searches, merged/general-menu searches and the cached overlap inventory were checked. The cache reports complete pagination for 598 open PRs and 6,683 Discussion records, with incomplete sparse local-note coverage. Arbitrary diffs and unpublished work remain outside that coverage.

Completion refresh listed all 191 account open PRs and inspected the fourteen other PRs created since the advance CLAIM, PR6648 through PR6662 excluding this PR. None studies this compatible-width chronological batching contract or computes a conflicting value for the same instance. PR6649 optimizes tensor-cut capacity per rank at a fixed tensor length; its multiplicities have a different objective and are not compared with invocation replication. No additional scientific computation checked another contribution.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks passed at exact head `bd728a5c8d09599072a98503ca7741d934ecfa74` in [run 41661667168](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41661667168): [plan](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41661667168/job/126006153906) in 7m55s and [replay (research/mixed-width-batching)](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41661667168/job/126011022447) in 1m20s. The completed checks were read once. Separate run metadata confirms completed success and the matching head.

Hosted replay confirms execution of the registered normal and optimized finite checks and package metadata validation. Local committed-byte/source-history and export checks also passed. The universal result rests on the written proof; independent human and formal proof-kernel acceptance are unclaimed. The physical menu and supplier-cost obligations remain open. The delivered scope matches the advance CLAIM. No failed or waived check remains.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated.

Seven new package files. Shared code, frozen predecessor evidence, credit lines and selected-frontier records are unchanged.
